dossier.architecture: Modular turret scorer with progressively simplified acquisition and interchangeable climb concepts.

subsystems.drivetrain: SDS swerve; modular structure supports repeated revisions.
subsystems.intake: Pneumatic flex-wheel design evolved to motorized roller pickup; bumper covering selected for ball grip.
subsystems.transfer: Two sensor-tracked chambers and compliant feed rollers; wrong-color cargo rejected through a slower shot.
subsystems.scoring: Over-360-degree turret and motorized adjustable hood; high camera mount retains near-goal target view.
subsystems.endgame: Dual gas-spring telescopes for traversal; separate passive high-bar prototype brought as an alternative, not assumed fielded.
subsystems.controls: Vision-corrected odometry, moving-shot compensation, intermediate pickup pose and gyro-based climb timing.

versions: Team reports four broad robot iterations. Removed pneumatics, changed intake contact material and replaced servo hood actuation with a motor.
dossier.analysis: Compare whole configurations: the lower-priority climb was designed around the scorer, and the team explicitly considered a faster, lower-scoring endgame when late-cycle output was valuable.
limits: Only published/reviewed configurations are established; further intermediate changes may be undocumented.

context_documents.body:
# 2022-4414: Repeated intake iterations must remain attached to the correct shooter snapshot

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

The team reports several whole-robot iterations. The retained account distinguishes early pneumatic flex-wheel collection from later motorized rollers, sensor-tracked cargo chambers, a wide-range turret and a high-mounted targeting camera.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The interview emphasizes rapid fabrication/iteration and material testing. More exact performance attribution requires the dated release/configuration, not the number of iterations alone.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

A camera mounted to preserve near-goal visibility changes the available aiming envelope. Color/rejection and staged possession must still coordinate with turret direction. Do not combine every photographed intake into one version.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Validate close-range sight lines, rejection trajectory and intake/feed readiness after a mechanism swap.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.

source_reviews.title: Behind the Bumpers with HighTide at Championship
source_reviews.locator: 1:34–4:03 manufacturing; 4:05–7:24 acquisition and hopper; 7:39–9:39 turret; 9:40–12:13 climbs; 12:20–15:45 controls
source_reviews.review_basis: Read the full available English automatic caption track, including the start and end. Technical details are attributed to team speakers. No visual inspection claimed.
facts: The collector moved from pneumatic four-bar actuation to electric chain and cross-shaft deployment, then to a wrapped aluminum roller for Championship.
The hopper has two sensed chambers and a later flex-wheel path. Wrong color uses a low-speed shooter release.
A motor and rack replaced linear servo hood actuation. A high-bar prototype remained distinct from the dual-telescope traversal setup.
source_reviews.limitations: Timing and repeatability are team claims. Prototypes and public photos cannot establish event-by-event fit.

source_reviews.title: HighTide interview follow-up
facts: Team identified a plate supporting the cantilevered climber from the rear drive rail without another cross tube.
source_reviews.limitations: The attachment dimensions and load ratings were not verified.

source_review.whole_robot_explanation: Cutback used a wide intake, two separately sensed holding spaces and a rotating launcher. Its frame made it possible to change the collector, hood and climb without remaking the entire machine. Access to in-house milling, routing, cutting and printing supported that pace. The successive intake revisions removed system weight and made the roller easier to replace, while later hood changes improved the movement of the scoring mechanism.
piece_flow: The deployed roller draws the ball across the bumper. Mecanum wheels and bent flaps bias its path into the hopper.
Flex-wheel contacts move cargo through two sensed chambers. Color logic can select a low-speed ejection through the launcher.
The turret aims, the motorized hood sets elevation, and separate speed setpoints govern the launch contacts.
source_review.packaging_and_motion: A single cross-shaft drives both sides of the intake deployment. The turret’s slightly more than one turn of travel provides overlap but still requires cable clearance and suitable routing. The rear climber support can cantilever from the drive rail according to the team’s follow-up, making that attachment part of the primary climb load path.

subsystems.name: Collector revision
subsystems.construction: Early pneumatic four-bar and flex wheels. Later Falcon-driven chain and cross-shaft, wrapped thin-wall aluminum roller and bent Lexan flaps.
subsystems.operation: Deploy both sides together, with an optional intermediate position for a bouncing ball. Draw the ball against the bumper into the next contacts.
subsystems.team_rationale: The team removed pneumatics when the intake was the remaining user. A wrapped tube was easier to replace than the spaced flex wheels. A grippier bumper fabric addressed slipping.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Treat the bumper and roller as a contact pair. Higher roller grip may do little if the bumper side slips, and a shared shaft may transmit an offset impact across the mechanism.
subsystems.interfaces: The deployed roller and biased flaps must hand off across the entire pickup width.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Check chain tension, bumper fabric wear, and a partial deployment after a hit.
subsystems.unknowns: Exact geometry and paired-ball reliability are open.

subsystems.name: Hopper and rejection
subsystems.construction: Two individually sensed spaces, flex-wheel transport and a configurable mounting plate.
subsystems.operation: Stage each cargo separately and route the wrong color through the launcher at lower speed.
subsystems.team_rationale: The flex-wheel array worked comparably to heavier accelerators in the team’s account. The plate made sensor changes easier.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Modular fastening is useful only if mounting and alignment references remain repeatable. Measure the disruption a rejected ball causes to the following correct one.
subsystems.interfaces: Both spaces converge on the shooter entry and share its ready state.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Verify sensor replacement without moving the feed axis and check clearance with paired arrivals.
subsystems.unknowns: No confirmed sensor dwell or reject trajectory.

subsystems.name: Turret and adjustable hood
subsystems.construction: Bearing stack and laser-cut gear features. Later Falcon and rack hood drive, with a top-mounted Limelight.
subsystems.operation: Aim across overlapping yaw limits and compensate for chassis movement using an aim offset.
subsystems.team_rationale: The team wanted to shoot while pinned and wanted faster hood positioning with better camera sight near the hub.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: A broad aim range has value when it buys release opportunities. It requires launch calibration, limit handling and cable management across the working sweep.
subsystems.interfaces: Odometry and camera corrections feed both shot selection and moving compensation.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Exercise wrap handling, lost vision and hood end stops, then check motion after repairs.
subsystems.unknowns: No reviewed shot logs or measured turret travel.

subsystems.name: Traversal and high-bar prototype
subsystems.construction: Dual telescopes with gas-assisted pivot in the traversal assembly. Separate prototype with passively deployed hook and surgical tubing.
subsystems.operation: Shift the loaded telescope outward to present the next hook. The alternate high-bar setup trades away traversal reach.
subsystems.team_rationale: The team retained traversal options at Championship, while investigating quick high hangs to preserve scoring time.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Compare net scoring value and the reliability of each entire endgame, including approach.
subsystems.interfaces: Modular rear attachments must support hang loads and clear the parked scorer.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Inspect the rail joint and fixture-test tilted capture and imperfect deployment.
subsystems.unknowns: Alternate prototype installation and verified cycle times are unresolved.

revisions: Pneumatics removed from intake; final roller wrap and flaps adopted; hood changed from linear servo to motor/rack.
transferable_principles: Maintain stable interfaces where build capacity permits rapid iteration.
Check bumper traction as part of the intake.
disconfirming_conditions: Modularity can cost mass and time where interfaces are hard to hold in alignment.
If aim opportunities remain plentiful with a fixed shooter, quantify whether the rotating assembly earns its cost.
remaining_gaps: Release timing, exact event installs, frame attachment loads and complete motion CAD.
recommended_images: Request the three intake versions and a rear-side view of the cantilever plate under the climber.
